# linux-builder

## nix.linux-builder.enable

Whether to enable a Linux builder: a NixOS container, run by
`virtualisation.oci-containers`, that builds
`systems` for this host’s Nix over SSH.

*Type:*
boolean

*Default:*

```nix
false
```

*Example:*

```nix
true
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)

## nix.linux-builder.package

The builder image, with `config` merged in through its
`override { modules = …; }`, as `packages/linux-builder-image`
takes. An aarch64-linux derivation: it builds on a Linux builder
this host already has, unless a substituter has it.

*Type:*
package

*Default:*

```nix
nixham.packages.${system}.linux-builder-image
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)

## nix.linux-builder.config

NixOS configuration of the builder, on top of the image’s base
profile. Its Nix settings (`nix.settings`,
`nix.extraOptions`) reach the builder at boot as
`NIX_CONFIG`, so changing only them reuses the image; anything else
rebuilds it. `NIX_CONFIG` is visible to `container inspect`:
use `nixConfSecretFile` for secrets.

CPUs, memory, Rosetta and SSH keys are the host’s, set here in
`nix.linux-builder`. No effect when `image` or
`imageFile` selects an image built out of band.

*Type:*
module

*Default:*

```nix
{ }
```

*Example:*

```nix
{ pkgs, ... }:
{
  nix.settings.substituters = [ "https://cache.example.org" ];
  environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.htop ];
}

```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)

## nix.linux-builder.ephemeral

Whether to enable an ephemeral store: without the `linux-builder-store` volume, the
builder’s store is lost every time it stops.

*Type:*
boolean

*Default:*

```nix
false
```

*Example:*

```nix
true
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)

## nix.linux-builder.imageFile

An OCI image archive, loaded when the builder starts unless its
`imageRef`, the ref the archive names, is already present. Its
loaded predecessors in `package`’s repository
(`linux-builder`) are deleted then. Excludes `image`.

*Type:*
null or package

*Default:*

```nix
if image == null then package else null
```

*Example:*

```nix
archive // { imageRef = "linux-builder:prebuilt"; }
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)

## nix.linux-builder.kernel

Guest kernel the builder boots, whatever the runtime’s default. It
must have `CONFIG_EROFS_FS` for the image’s `/etc`, and `CONFIG_KVM`
for `kvm` builds, and hold `vmlinux-arm64`.

*Type:*
package

*Default:*

```nix
nixham.packages.${system}.apple-container-kernel
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)

## nix.linux-builder.nixConfSecretFile

Runtime path of a nix.conf for the builder’s secrets, e.g.
`access-tokens`, included last. It is mounted read-only into the
builder, so `container inspect` shows its path, never its
contents. The primary user, whose runtime mounts it, must be able to
read it.

*Type:*
null or string

*Default:*

```nix
null
```

*Example:*

```nix
"/run/secrets/linux-builder-nix.conf"
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)

## nix.linux-builder.onDemand.enable

Start the builder on Nix’s first connection, to
``` 127.0.0.1: `` onDemand.port ```, and stop it once idle, as
`virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.apple-container.onDemand`,
which sets the timeouts; its `idleTimeout` defaults to 0 here, so the
builder stops once no connection is open. When off, the builder runs from login and
is reached by name, through the runtime’s default DNS domain.

*Type:*
boolean

*Default:*

```nix
true
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)

## nix.linux-builder.onDemand.port

Loopback port Nix connects to, which starts the builder.

*Type:*
16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)

*Default:*

```nix
22022
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)

## nix.linux-builder.sshKeyFile

Runtime path of the SSH private key root’s Nix logs in with, never
copied to the store. The default is generated at activation.
Activation authorizes its public half for `sshUser`.

*Type:*
string

*Default:*

```nix
"/var/lib/linux-builder/ssh_key"
```

*Example:*

```nix
"/run/secrets/linux-builder-ssh-key"
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)

## nix.linux-builder.userSshKeyFile

Runtime path of an SSH private key for users other than root, e.g.
readable by a group allowed to build on the builder; when null, only
root can. Activation authorizes its public half too. A file of its
own: ssh refuses a key that others can read, so
`sshKeyFile` can’t be shared.

*Type:*
null or string

*Default:*

```nix
null
```

*Example:*

```nix
"/run/secrets/linux-builder-ssh-key-users"
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)

## nix.linux-builder.virtualization

Expose virtualization to the builder, for `kvm` and `nixos-test`
builds, as
`virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.apple-container.virtualization`.
It needs an M3 or later: on older hosts the builder fails to start,
so turn it off.

*Type:*
boolean

*Default:*

```nix
true
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/nix/linux-builder/default.nix)
